D3 WBB 2026-27 Published Schedules

361 published schedules of 411 teams · difficulty ranks and at-large buffer vs. preseason rankings · unpublished teams always sort last

Some nonconference opponents are not locked in stone: they come from tournaments, and Scott has taken a best guess.

Projected NPI: every game goes to the better preseason rank. Each team's starting NPI is the NPI that last season's team at the same rank finished with (preseason #40 starts at the NPI last season's #40 finished with). Teams with no published schedule have no games to project, so they keep that starting NPI. Wins needed is the average win value that lands on last season's last at-large NPI (59.15, St. Mary's (MN)) after the team's projected losses, shown as the opponent rank a single win of that value requires. Projected field: the best preseason rank in each conference takes the AQ (43), the next 21 by projected NPI are at-large; last at-large UW-La Crosse, first out Mt. Union.

Caveats: the at-large buffer is a simplistic estimate made against each team's aggregate average schedule strength; it ignores the distribution of that schedule and the dynamics of the NPI formula, which the projected NPI does account for. The projected NPI is simplistic in its own way: it rests almost entirely on Scott's preseason rankings, with every game decided by rank and no allowance for upsets, injuries, or in-season change.

How to read a card: what each value is and the assumptions behind it
Preseason #N
Scott's projected preseason rank, 1 to 411. Every projection on this page starts from it.
Overall difficulty
Rank of the schedule among the 361 published schedules by average opponent strength; #1 is the hardest. Tag: Strong = top 15% of published schedules, Above avg = top 35%, Middling = top 55%, Weak = the rest.
Conf difficulty
The same ranking using conference games only.
NonConf difficulty
The same ranking using nonconference games only.
Avg opp rank
Average preseason rank of every scheduled opponent.
At-large buffer
Losses the team can absorb and still sit in at-large position: the safe-loss threshold rounded down to the dangerous threshold rounded down, never below 0. Simplistic: estimated against the team's aggregate average schedule strength, ignoring the distribution of that schedule and the dynamics of the NPI formula.
Toughest nonconf
The three best-ranked nonconference opponents by preseason rank. The counts are games against opponents in the preseason top 100 and top 200, conference games included; color and underline show where each count ranks among published schedules using the difficulty cutoffs (double underline = strong, solid = above avg, dashed = middling, dotted = weak). Tournament opponents are a best guess.
Projected NPI · #rank · W-L
Every scheduled game goes to the better preseason rank. Each team's starting NPI is the NPI that last season's team at the same rank finished with (preseason #40 starts at the NPI last season's #40 finished with). From there the real NPI formula iterates to convergence over the published schedules (the top 15 wins always count, further wins only at or above the team's own NPI, and losses below it). Teams with no published schedule have no games to project, so they keep their starting NPI. Rank is among all 411 teams. Simplistic: it rests on preseason rankings only, with no allowance for upsets, injuries, or in-season change.
Bid pill
AQ-n: the best preseason rank in each conference (43 conferences). AL-n: the next 21 by projected NPI. #k overall is seed order within the field; nth team out is order outside it. Last at-large UW-La Crosse, first out Mt. Union.
Wins must avg V (a #R opponent) · scheduled avg S
V is the value the team's counting wins must average so that, after its projected losses, the season NPI lands on last season's last at-large NPI (59.15, St. Mary's (MN)). R is the deepest-ranked opponent whose single win is worth V on last season's NPI-by-rank curve. S is the projected mean value of the counting wins. Color: S minus V of 2 or more is green, 0 or more blue, -2 or more yellow, below that red. Out of reach means V exceeds a win over the #1 team.
Starting NPI · no schedule
An unpublished team has no games to project, so it keeps its starting NPI. Each team's starting NPI is the NPI that last season's team at the same rank finished with (preseason #40 starts at the NPI last season's #40 finished with). It can still hold a bid. Unpublished cards have a dashed outline and always sort last.
Scatter plot
Preseason rank against safe at-large losses (the unrounded safe-loss threshold), so it carries the same simplification as the buffer.
